settings.name_in_paper: Repeated strategic classification against delta-BMR agents (Stackelberg regret)
unmapped: Actions are linear classifiers (hyperplane normals) in A subset of [-1,1]^{d+1}; loss is binary 0-1 loss on the agent's reported feature vector
Agents are delta-bounded myopically rational: they best-respond to the committed classifier by misreporting within a delta-ball of their true feature vector; true feature vector never observed
Regret is Stackelberg regret: comparator evaluated against agent best responses to the comparator action
Learner knows delta; feedback is the reported vector and label, which reveals the loss of all actions outside a 4 sqrt(d) delta band
Algorithm requires access to an in-probability oracle and polytope volume computation

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated strategic classification against delta-BMR agents (Stackelberg regret) (lower bound)
unmapped: Linear classifiers with binary loss against delta-BMR strategic agents; Stackelberg regret
Hard instance uses truthful agents and labels drawn i.i.d. Bernoulli per phase

source.label: thm:regr-grind
source.quote: Given a finite horizon $T$ the Stackelberg regret incurred by $\grinder$ (Algo.~\ref{algo:grinding}) is: \calR(T) \leq \calO \left( \sqrt{T \cdot \log \left(T\cdot\frac{\lambda\left( \calA \right)}{\lambda\left(\up\right)}\right) \cdot \log \left(\frac{\lambda\left( \calA \right)}{\lambda\left(\up\right)}\right)}\right) where by $\lambda(A)$ we denote the Lebesgue measure ...

results.notes: Data-dependent bound (depends on algorithm-induced partition). Proof takes expectations over the algorithm's randomness; regret type not explicitly stated. Paper notes polytope volume computation is #P-hard (information-theoretic result); with volume oracle runtime O(T^d) (Lemma B.8). Doubling trick removes knowledge of T and lambda(p_delta).

symbols.eps_or: approximation accuracy of the in-probability oracle (multiplicative)
symbols.C_O: unspecified constant hidden in the O(.) of the first term

conditions: access to an eps-approximate in-probability oracle with eps <= 1/2
tuning: eta = gamma tuned as in Theorem 4.1

source.label: lem:apx-oracle
source.quote: For $\eps \leq 1/2$, we call {\upshape $\tPr_t[\alpha_t]$} an $\eps$-approximation oracle to $\Prin[\alpha_t]$, if $|\tPr_t [\alpha_t] - \Prin[\alpha_t] | \leq \eps \Prin[\alpha_t]$. Then, $\grinder$ run with oracle $\tPr_t[\cdot]$ instead of $\Prin[\alpha_t]$ achieves Stackelberg regret $\calR(T) \leq \calO(\sqrt{ T \log (T \lambda(\calA)/\lambda(\up))\cdot \log (\lambda(\calA)/\lambda(\up))}) + 2 \eps T$.

results.notes: Mixed O-term plus explicit 2 eps T; recorded with explicit constant C_O. Main text says rate preserved when eps <= 1/sqrt(T).

results.notes: Regret with min outside expectation, i.e. pseudo-regret style Stackelberg regret. Log base not specified (phases Phi = log ratio with 2^kappa normalization).

conditions: fixed feature vector x=(u)^d with u in [1/4,3/4], truthful agents, labels i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2 +/- eps) under one of two environments U, L

source.label: lem:sqrt
source.quote: Fix a $\vr = \vx = (u)^d$ ... There exists a utility model for the agents, and a pair of adversarial environments $U$ and $L$ such that ... \max_{\nu \in \{U,L\}} \min_{\alphast \in \calA} \E_{\nu} \left[\sum_{t \in [T]} \ell(\alpha_t, \vr_t(\alpha_t),y_t) - \sum_{t \in [T]} \ell(\alphast,\vr_t(\alphast),y_t) \right] \geq \frac{1}{9\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{T}
